slides.title: Three Steps to a Formula
slides.kicker: Valencies criss-cross and your formula is ready!
bullets: Writing a covalent formula starts by writing the symbols of the constituent elements of the compound.
Next, write the valency of each element, referring to Table 9.1 of the book.
Finally, crossover the valencies of the combining atoms and write them as subscripts after the symbols.

items: Write the valencies of both elements

slides.note: Simple teen-step recipe, works every time!

slides.title: HCl and H2S by Crossover
slides.kicker: Same method, two compounds, zero confusion!
bullets: Hydrogen chloride: hydrogen has valency 1 and chlorine has valency 1, so crossover gives the formula HCl.
Hydrogen sulfide: hydrogen has valency 1 and sulfur has valency 2, so the formula becomes H2S.
A valency of 1 is never written as a subscript; only numbers above 1 appear in the formula.
slides.note: Sulfur ka 2 hydrogen ke upar chala gaya!

slides.title: CCl4: Carbon Checks In
bullets: Carbon has valency 4 and chlorine has valency 1, so crossover places 4 under Cl and 1 under C.
The formula that comes out is CCl4, which is carbon tetrachloride.
One crossover table can handle any covalent compound once the valencies are known.

slides.title: Criss-Cross the Charges
bullets: Write the symbol of the cation first, followed by the symbol of the anion.
Write the charges under the symbols rather than as superscripts, then crossover only the numbers.
The chemical formula must give the simplest ratio of elements, so divide subscripts by a common factor if any.
If you get subscripts 2 and 4, divide both by 2 to get 1 and 2 for the final formula.

slides.title: CaCl2, Al2O3 and MgO
slides.kicker: Two chlorides per calcium, charges balanced!
bullets: Calcium chloride: Ca is 2+ and Cl is 1-, so criss-crossing gives CaCl2, two chloride ions per calcium ion.
Aluminium oxide: Al is 3+ and O is 2-, so the criss-crossed formula is Al2O3.
Magnesium oxide: the two valencies are the same, giving Mg2O2, which is simply written as MgO.
Positive and negative charges must balance each other, and the overall structure must be neutral.
slides.note: Mg2O2 ko simplify karke MgO likha!

slides.title: Brackets for Polyatomic Ions
slides.kicker: Bracket ka magic: Al(OH)3, not AlOH3!
bullets: Magnesium hydroxide has two hydroxide ions, OH-, for each magnesium ion, Mg2+, giving Mg(OH)2.
Use brackets when two or more polyatomic ions of the same type appear in a formula.
In aluminium hydroxide, the bracket around OH with subscript 3 shows three hydroxide ions on one aluminium ion.
Calcium carbonate CaCO3 and aluminium sulfate Al2(SO4)3 show that brackets follow the polyatomic ion, never a single atom.

slides.title: Activity 9.4: Test Time
slides.kicker: Paani, kerosene, petrol: kaun ghulta hai?
bullets: Collect samples of camphor, sodium chloride, copper sulfate, sugar and naphthalene for testing.
Try dissolving each sample separately in water, kerosene and petrol, and record observations in Table 9.2.
For conductivity, fix two carbon or metal electrodes through cardboard and connect them to a 9 V battery and a light bulb.
Safety first: never touch connected electrodes, and remember petrol and kerosene are flammable.

items: Test conductivity of solid and solution

slides.note: Low-voltage battery use karo, safe raho!

slides.title: Solubility Splits Families
slides.kicker: Water loves ions, kerosene loves camphor!
bullets: Ionic compounds like sodium chloride and copper sulfate are generally soluble in water but insoluble in kerosene and petrol.
Most covalent compounds, such as camphor and naphthalene, are insoluble in water but dissolve in kerosene and petrol.
Testing where a compound dissolves is a quick way to guess which family it belongs to.
slides.note: Solvent hi family bata deta hai!

slides.title: Why Solid Salt Is Silent
slides.kicker: Fixed ions: no current. Free ions: glow!
bullets: Ionic compounds do not conduct electricity in the solid state because their ions are held in fixed positions by strong forces.
To conduct electricity, ions must be free to move, which happens when sodium chloride or copper sulfate dissolves in water.
Sugar is soluble in water but does not provide ions in solution, so it does not conduct electricity; camphor and naphthalene also do not.
Strong inter-ionic forces give ionic compounds generally high melting and boiling points.
slides.note: Molten state mein kya hoga? Socho!

slides.title: Adding Up Molecular Mass
slides.kicker: Formula mila? Masses add karo, done!
bullets: Once you know the formula of a covalent compound, you can find the mass of its molecules.
Molecular mass is found by simply adding up the masses of the atoms present in the molecule.
Take the atomic mass of each element and multiply it by the number of atoms of that element in the formula.

items: Multiply by the number of atoms

slides.title: Water 18 u, CO2 44 u
slides.kicker: Do worked examples from the book!
bullets: Water H2O: atomic masses H = 1 u and O = 16 u, so molecular mass = (1 u x 2) + (16 u x 1) = 18 u.
Carbon dioxide CO2: atomic masses C = 12 u and O = 16 u, so molecular mass = (12 u x 1) + (16 u x 2) = 44 u.
The unit u is used for both atomic mass and molecular mass in these calculations.
slides.note: 18 u aur 44 u, yaad kar lo!

slides.title: Ionic Compounds: No Molecules
bullets: In ionic compounds, the ions form 3-D crystals, so ionic compounds do not form molecules.
That is why we do not calculate a molecular mass for sodium chloride or copper sulfate.
For ionic compounds we use the formula unit mass instead, which the next section explains.
slides.note: Solid salt ek crystal hai, molecule nahi!

slides.title: What Is a Formula Unit
slides.kicker: Simplest ratio of ions = formula unit!
bullets: In ionic compounds, the collection of the simplest whole number ratio of ions is termed a formula unit.
The mass of a formula unit is called the formula unit mass.
It is calculated by adding the atomic masses of all the atoms present in a formula unit.
slides.note: Sodium oxide ka formula unit: Na2O!

slides.title: Na2O Weighs 62 u
slides.kicker: Book ka Example 9.6, step by step!
bullets: Sodium oxide Na2O: atomic masses Na = 23 u and O = 16 u.
Formula unit mass of Na2O = (23 u x 2) + (16 u x 1) = 62 u.
Calcium nitrate Ca(NO3)2: with Ca = 40 u, N = 14 u, O = 16 u, it is 40 + 2 x (14 + 48) = 164 u.

items: Multiply each by its atom count

slides.title: Which Mass for Which?
slides.kicker: Covalent? Molecular mass. Ionic? Formula unit!
bullets: Covalent compounds form molecules, so we calculate their molecular mass, like 18 u for water.
Ionic compounds form 3-D crystals of ions, so we calculate their formula unit mass, like 62 u for sodium oxide.
Understanding atoms, molecules and bonding reveals the hidden science behind everything we use each day.
slides.note: Tiny atoms build the whole universe!

flashcards.front: What three steps give the formula of a covalent compound?
flashcards.back: Write the element symbols, write their valencies, then crossover the valencies as subscripts after the symbols.

flashcards.front: Why is the formula of hydrogen sulfide H2S?
flashcards.back: Sulfur has valency 2, so crossover puts 2 under hydrogen, while the valency 1 of hydrogen is not written.

flashcards.front: Carbon valency 4 and chlorine valency 1 give which formula?
flashcards.back: Crossover gives CCl4, carbon tetrachloride, with four chlorine atoms around one carbon atom.

flashcards.front: Whose symbol is written first in an ionic compound formula?
flashcards.back: The cation first, followed by the anion; then the charges, only the numbers, are criss-crossed.

flashcards.front: Why does calcium chloride have the formula CaCl2?
flashcards.back: Ca is 2+ and Cl is 1-, so two chloride ions balance one calcium ion and the structure stays neutral.

flashcards.front: When are brackets used in an ionic formula?
flashcards.back: When two or more polyatomic ions of the same type appear, as in Mg(OH)2 or Al(OH)3.

flashcards.front: Are ionic compounds soluble in kerosene or petrol?
flashcards.back: No. Sodium chloride and copper sulfate dissolve in water but stay insoluble in kerosene and petrol.

flashcards.front: Why does solid sodium chloride not conduct electricity?
flashcards.back: Its ions are held in fixed positions by strong forces; ions must be free to move to conduct.

flashcards.front: Sugar dissolves in water, yet its solution does not conduct. Why?
flashcards.back: Sugar provides no ions in solution, and freely moving ions are needed to carry electric current.
The mass of a molecule, found by adding up the masses of all the atoms present in it.

flashcards.front: Molecular mass of CO2 with C = 12 u and O = 16 u?
Molecular mass of water with H = 1 u and O = 16 u?
What is a formula unit in an ionic compound?
flashcards.back: The collection of the simplest whole number ratio of ions in the compound.

flashcards.front: Formula unit mass of Na2O with Na = 23 u, O = 16 u?

quiz.q: What is the first step when writing the chemical formula of a covalent compound?
options: Write the symbols of the constituent elements
Write the molecular mass of the compound
Crossover the charges of the ions
Count the ions present in a crystal
quiz.why: Step one of the crossover method is writing the symbols of the constituent elements.

quiz.q: Hydrogen has valency 1 and sulfur has valency 2. Using crossover, the formula of hydrogen sulfide is:
quiz.why: Sulfur's valency 2 crosses under H and hydrogen's 1 is not written, giving H2S.

quiz.q: Carbon has valency 4 and chlorine has valency 1. Crossover of the valencies gives which formula?
quiz.why: Crossover places 4 under Cl and 1 under C, so the formula is CCl4.

quiz.q: While writing the formula of an ionic compound, which ion is written first?
quiz.why: Step one says write the symbol of the cation first, followed by the anion.

quiz.q: Magnesium is 2+ and oxygen is 2-. Criss-crossing and simplifying gives which formula?
quiz.why: Criss-cross gives Mg2O2, and dividing by the common factor 2 gives MgO.

quiz.q: Why is the formula of aluminium hydroxide written Al(OH)3 and not AlOH3?
options: Because OH is a diatomic gas
The bracket with subscript 3 shows three hydroxide ions bound to one aluminium ion
Because aluminium can bond only three times in total
quiz.why: Brackets are used when two or more polyatomic ions of the same type appear in a formula.

quiz.q: In Activity 9.4, which compounds were found to be soluble in water?
quiz.why: Ionic compounds like sodium chloride and copper sulfate are generally soluble in water.

quiz.q: Solid sodium chloride does not conduct electricity because:
options: Its ions are held in fixed positions by strong forces
It contains no charged particles at all
Solids can never carry electric current
quiz.why: To conduct, ions must be free to move; in the solid they are held in fixed positions.

quiz.q: Predict: which type of compound would conduct electricity in the molten state?
options: Neither type can ever conduct when melted
Ionic compounds, since their ions become free to move
quiz.why: Conduction needs freely moving ions; melting frees the ions locked in the solid.

quiz.q: The molecular mass of a covalent compound is found by:
options: Counting the molecules in a sample
Adding the masses of the atoms present in the molecule
Multiplying the valencies of the elements
quiz.why: The book defines it as simply adding up the masses of the atoms present in the molecule.

quiz.q: Using C = 12 u and O = 16 u, the molecular mass of carbon dioxide is:
quiz.why: (12 u x 1) + (16 u x 2) = 44 u, as worked in Example 9.5.

quiz.q: Why do we not calculate a molecular mass for sodium chloride?
options: Ionic compounds form 3-D crystals of ions, not molecules
Its atoms are too heavy to add up
Chlorine is a gas, so mass is undefined
Sodium chloride has no chemical formula
quiz.why: In ionic compounds the ions form 3-D crystals, so they do not form molecules.

quiz.q: In an ionic compound, a formula unit is:
options: The simplest whole number ratio of ions
One full crystal of the compound
quiz.why: The book defines the formula unit as the simplest whole number ratio of ions.

quiz.q: Using Na = 23 u and O = 16 u, the formula unit mass of sodium oxide is:
quiz.why: (23 u x 2) + (16 u x 1) = 62 u, as worked in Example 9.6.

quiz.q: Using Ca = 40 u, N = 14 u, O = 16 u, the formula unit mass of Ca(NO3)2 is:
quiz.why: 40 + 2 x (14 + 48) = 164 u, as worked in Example 9.7.

examples.title: Crossover Builds Hydrogen Sulfide
examples.problem: Write the chemical formula of hydrogen sulfide. The valency of hydrogen is 1 and the valency of sulfur is 2.
steps: Write the symbols of the two elements: H and S.
Write the valencies under the symbols: hydrogen 1, sulfur 2.
Crossover the valencies: sulfur's 2 becomes the subscript of H, and hydrogen's 1 becomes the subscript of S.
A subscript of 1 is not written, so only the 2 on H remains.
examples.answer: The formula of hydrogen sulfide is H2S.

examples.title: Aluminium Sulfate with Brackets
examples.problem: The aluminium ion is Al with charge 3+ and the sulfate ion is SO4 with charge 2-. Write the chemical formula of aluminium sulfate.
steps: Write the cation first, then the anion: Al and SO4.
Write the charges under the symbols: 3+ and 2-.
Criss-cross only the numbers: 2 becomes the subscript of Al, and 3 becomes the subscript of SO4.
SO4 is a polyatomic ion, so enclose it in brackets before writing the subscript 3.
examples.answer: The formula of aluminium sulfate is Al2(SO4)3.

examples.title: Molecular Mass of Nitric Acid
examples.problem: Find the molecular mass of nitric acid, HNO3, given atomic masses H = 1 u, N = 14 u and O = 16 u.
steps: Count the atoms in HNO3: 1 hydrogen, 1 nitrogen and 3 oxygen atoms.
examples.answer: The molecular mass of nitric acid is 63 u.

examples.title: Formula Unit Mass of Mg(OH)2
examples.problem: Find the formula unit mass of magnesium hydroxide, Mg(OH)2, given atomic masses Mg = 24 u, O = 16 u and H = 1 u.
steps: Mg(OH)2 contains 1 magnesium ion, 2 oxygen atoms and 2 hydrogen atoms.
examples.answer: The formula unit mass of magnesium hydroxide is 58 u.
